title: White House announces Black Sea ceasefire after Riyadh talks as Russia sets conditions
body:
On 25 March 2025, the White House said that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to a ceasefire in the Black Sea. The announcement followed talks held earlier that week in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, where US officials met separately with Ukrainian and Russian delegations.

The Kremlin issued its own statement attaching preconditions. These included lifting limits on agricultural exports, since Russia is a major wheat producer, and reconnecting Russian banks to the SWIFT global payments system. The report did not say when the truce would take effect.

Analysts quoted by Bloomberg said the agreements reached so far were piecemeal. They said Russia's demands raised concern that Moscow was playing for time to see what concessions it could obtain. US officials were working to fulfil President Donald Trump's campaign promise to end the war.

The Riyadh talks came two weeks after the US-Ukrainian meeting in Jeddah on 11 March, at which Ukraine had accepted a US proposal for a 30-day ceasefire along the whole front line. Moscow had repeatedly rejected freezing hostilities along the current front line.
